METALWORK — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #3
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: METALWORK
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Metalwork 2.1 Hand tools and bench.

2. When learning Safety in the workshop, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Safety in the workshop.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Safety in the workshop.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Safety in the workshop.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Safety in the workshop.

3. When learning Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictoria.

4. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Run with the tool
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Remove all guards

5. When learning Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork 1.2 Safety at workshop 2.0 Tools and materials in Meta.

6. When learning Introduction to Metalwork, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Introduction to Metalwork.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Introduction to Metalwork.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Introduction to Metalwork.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Introduction to Metalwork.

7. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. Internal Cooking Timer
   B. Information and Communication Technology
   C. International Cricket Team
   D. Input Cable Tester

8. When learning Measuring and marking out tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools.

9. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. Speaker
   C. CPU
   D. Monitor

10. When learning Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Scales and conventions 3.2 Pictorial drawing 4.0 Metal joining and finishing pro.

11. When learning Hand tools and bench tools, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools.

12. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

13. When learning Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.

14. When learning Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 , the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ferrous and non-ferrous metals 2.4 Project 3.0 Related drawing in Metalwork 3.1 .

15. When learning Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Ferrous and Non- ferrous metals.

16. When learning Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Hand tools and bench tools 2.2 Measuring and marking out tools 2.3 Ferrous and n.

----

18. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Metalwork and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
